walkthroughs.body_html:
Education with Theory & Methods — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Education with Theory & Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Education with Theory & Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Marx
Durkheim
Parsons

mcqs.q: What does Parsons mean by 'meritocracy' in education?
options: Rewards and roles are allocated based on individual achievement.
Only middle-class students can succeed.
Topics removed from the syllabus.
Everyone gets equal outcomes regardless of effort.
Topics removed from the syllabus.
Secret lessons teachers deliberately hide from students.
Only middle-class students can succeed.
The unspoken norms, values, and behaviours taught implicitly in schools.

mcqs.q: Why do positivists prefer quantitative methods?
options: Because they hate qualitative research.

They produce objective, reliable, generalisable data resembling natural science.
Because numbers are easier to collect than words.
